A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TPP-SD and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite added sections and changed pagination.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 and Appendix C report original experiments on sampling fidelity, runtime, draft length, and draft model size using synthetic and real datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds draft-only sampling and Poisson-draft comparisons in Appendix D.2–D.3, Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: The default Transformer architecture, training objective, verification procedure, and adjusted-distribution sampling remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 adds an optional Poisson-draft variant, replacing neural autoregressive drafting with jointly generated exponential intervals and categorical marks fitted by maximum likelihood.

E1.justification: Both versions use Poisson, Hawkes, and Multi-Hawkes synthetic data and Taobao, Amazon, Taxi, and StackOverflow real data. The added comparisons reuse these datasets without introducing different tasks, populations, or input conditions.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens comparison with cheaper alternatives. Table 5 adds standalone autoregressive sampling from the small THP draft model across all seven datasets. Table 6 compares neural-draft TPP-SD with Poisson-draft TPP-SD on five datasets. Neither alternative was empirically compared in v1.

E3.justification: Existing splits, sampling horizons, metrics, training budgets, and default model sizes are retained. Appendix D adds targeted controls: standalone sampling from a one-head, one-layer THP and a Poisson-draft comparison using a THP target with maximum-likelihood rate and mark estimates. These extend the evaluation design without revising the original protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2–D.3 adds two substantive diagnostic studies: whether the small draft alone provides sufficient sampling fidelity, and whether inexpensive Poisson drafting compensates for lower acceptance. These address previously untested practical alternatives. Existing draft-length and draft-size ablations and distributional consistency plots remain.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly identifies variability shown in experimental figures as standard deviations across runs; v1 describes error bands without identifying their type. Existing three-seed table averages, five-seed ablations, and 95% KS bands remain unchanged. No increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values, while Tables 5–6 add substantial results for the new alternatives. Table 6 reports Poisson-versus-neural draft speedups of 5.430 versus 2.113 on Hawkes, but 2.230 versus 3.550 on Amazon. Table 5 also reports Taxi AR-target likelihood discrepancy as 0.441, conflicting with 1.4411 retained in Table 2.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and the mathematical derivations and proofs in Appendix A are retained without substantive correction or extension. The added Poisson parameter estimates specify standard fitting operations for the experimental variant rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adapting speculative decoding to Transformer TPPs, preserving the target sampling distribution, and achieving approximately 2–6 times acceleration. The added experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: New discussions argue that larger targets provide fidelity unavailable from the small draft alone and explain Poisson-draft speed through drafting cost versus acceptance rate. Existing limitations are retained. Interpretation is inconsistent: Table 6's caption claims a fidelity sacrifice, whereas Section D.3 says fidelity is maintained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code link in the abstract and statements about supplemental code, data, and documentation. Appendix D.3 specifies Poisson rate estimation, empirical mark probabilities, and simultaneous candidate generation. Existing hardware, optimizer, embedding dimensions, and training-budget disclosures remain unchanged; linked resources were not independently verified.

R1.justification: Six cited works are added, including additional Hawkes and neural TPP references. Section 3 newly acknowledges parallel inverse-map sampling in Shchur et al.'s triangular-map work. This improves coverage of relevant predecessors without substantially restructuring the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely unchanged. v3 adds a coauthor, conference identification, acknowledgments, a NeurIPS checklist, and two appendix discussion subsections, with corresponding renumbering and small wording and cross-reference edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–6 and enlarges Figure 2. Existing figures retain their underlying graphical content, and Tables 1–4 retain their structure and values. Caption edits and page reflow accompany the additions without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Tables 5–6 address practical alternatives left untested in v1, strengthening the rationale for target-model sampling and informing draft selection. Code-access information and clarification of plotted uncertainty also help. The gains are limited by the conflicting fidelity interpretations around Table 6 and the inconsistent Taxi baseline in Tables 2 and 5; the central method, proofs, and original benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
